filename: A Framework for Hybrid Physics-AI Coupled Ocean Models.pdf
title: A Framework for Hybrid Physics-AI Coupled Ocean Models
processes: ocean surface boundary layer vertical mixing
parameterization_target: Ocean boundary layer diffusivity, subgrid mesoscale eddy momentum stress tensor, and sea-ice concentration bias correction increment
testbed_rationale: Comprehensive benchmark and testbed for online-coupled ocean parameterizations (vertical mixing and mesoscale eddies) and sea ice bias corrections implemented in MOM6/OM4 and SPEAR, with open source code and Zenodo datasets available.
pain_points: Computational and memory bottlenecks during online CPU inference for deep CNN models, requiring GPU-based inference or knowledge distillation
Boundary artifacts and extrapolation errors near complex coastlines and land boundaries with fixed stencils
Lack of bitwise reproducibility unless specifically engineered in Fortran matrix multiplication modules
Generalization degradation when moving from forced ocean/ice setups to fully coupled atmosphere-ocean models due to atmospheric feedback triggering runaway convective/ice-albedo feedbacks
Compensating model errors: improving physical parameterizations does not always reduce overall climate biases
extraction_notes: The manuscript describes a comprehensive framework and multiple deployed models developed by the M2LInES collaboration, comparing CNNs, physics-aware ANNs, and equation discovery within MOM6/SIS2/SPEAR.
